title: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service

tasks.short: Separate restricted incoming mail, open permitted envelopes, and seal prepared outgoing mail.

steps.what: Separate incoming envelopes marked personal, confidential, or requiring special handling.
Open permitted envelopes by hand or opener, checking for retained contents.
Seal checked outgoing envelopes by hand or with a sealing machine.

tasks.design: Keep approved opening rules in the {DOCS} and use consistent physical trays for restricted and permitted mail. Standardise envelope stock and configure existing sealing equipment for routine outgoing batches; the clerk retains opening decisions and physical handling.
tasks.previous_blocker: Opening and sealing are physical operations. Confidential markings, mixed envelope sizes, and fragile contents limit unattended processing.
tasks.enabler_now: Clearer rules, standard materials, and existing equipment settings offer modest gains now. AI coding adds little to the physical operation itself.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous confidentiality markings, damaged envelopes, concealed enclosures, and equipment jams. Scanning after opening does not eliminate opening.
tasks.human_edge: Respect handling restrictions and recognise when an envelope should remain unopened or receive special treatment.
tasks.altitude: The week changes little: the clerk still opens and seals physical mail. Standard batches reduce some handling, with no additional decision rights.

Feed items through the meter or physically attach the required postage.
Check postage placement and legibility, separating spoiled or incorrect items for correction.

tasks.still_hard: Mixed item sizes, unusual destinations, poor impressions, and incompatible equipment limit savings.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsuitable packaging, sensitive documents, and service requirements that the dispatch request leaves unclear.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes into tariff selection and repeated entry. Physical preparation remains most of the task, and spending authority does not change.

tasks.short: Check mail addresses, postage and physical condition, and resolve items that cannot be processed.

steps.what: Read the address and check that required delivery details are present.
Check weight, service and postage using the postage meter in {OTHER}.
Inspect the packaging, closure and visible damage.
Hold unsuitable items and send the sender a correction request.
Confirm corrected delivery details, service or packaging instructions.

tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently valid item is unsuitable for processing and obtain the sender's intended correction.

tasks.short: Sort mail into destination bins or sacks and attach identifying tags.

steps.what: Read the destination and decide the appropriate internal route or dispatch group.

loop.input: Address image for an item without a recognised routing code.
loop.output: Visible recipient and destination text, with uncertain fields marked.
loop.check: Require source-image traceability and an unambiguous match against the approved routing directory. The clerk confirms the destination before placement.
loop.stop: One extraction attempt per item. Missing, ambiguous or unmatched text goes to manual reading; never guess a recipient.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use exact routing-code matches first. Mixed printed and handwritten address text needs extraction; rules alone cannot read all remaining items.

steps.what: Place the item into the selected bin or sack.
Write a destination and collection identifier on the bin or sack tag.
Attach the identifying tag to the matching bin or sack.

tasks.design: Use a routing table in {WORKFLOW}, fed by a limited recipient-location extract from {HCM}, and match routing codes deterministically. For uncoded items, a bounded extraction loop proposes a destination for clerk confirmation; print reusable destination tags through a label printer in {OTHER}. Physical placement and tag attachment remain manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recipient knowledge sits with experienced clerks, addresses vary, and physical sorting limits the value of software alone.
tasks.enabler_now: A small routing application and tag generator are straightforward to build. Bounded image extraction can assist with residual address text while leaving routing confirmation with the clerk.
tasks.still_hard: Outdated recipient locations, shared names, confidential addressees and wrong-bin placement remain difficult. Capture effort may outweigh reading savings at low volumes.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous recipients and recognise mail that needs restricted handling.

ambition.what: Temporary cover staff who need to sort mail without memorising internal routes.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time writing tags and recalling destinations, and more time resolving unclear items. The role can propose routing-directory corrections; employee-location changes remain with the authorised records owner.

tasks.statement: Place incoming or outgoing letters or packages into sacks or bins based on destination or type, and place identifying tags on sacks or bins.

tasks.short: Stop mail equipment, clear permitted jams safely and verify that operation can resume.

steps.what: Stop and isolate the equipment according to the approved procedure.
Inspect the accessible mail path and locate the obstruction.
Check the operating instructions for permitted recovery or maintenance escalation.
Remove accessible jammed mail, or leave equipment isolated for maintenance.
Check guards, authorise restart and test the cleared equipment.

tasks.design: Configure an equipment-specific index in {DOCS} that opens the approved recovery procedure and maintenance contact. Keep isolation, physical clearance and restart with authorised people; no generated repair advice or remote restart is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most time is spent inspecting and handling equipment. Instructions may also be difficult to find at the machine.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document links and search can shorten instruction lookup. No model or technical breakthrough is required.
tasks.still_hard: Equipment condition and safe access must be assessed locally. Some jams require a maintenance technician.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the obstruction exceeds operator training and stop the recovery attempt.
tasks.altitude: Instruction lookup becomes shorter, but physical work and restart authority stay with authorised staff. Nothing else changes in the person's decision rights.

reach.task: Investigate recurring equipment interruptions.
reach.learn: Fault categorisation, maintenance escalation and equipment service records.

evidence.claim: An approved procedure index can reduce lookup effort; it cannot physically clear equipment or establish safe restart conditions.

tasks.statement: Clear jams in sortation equipment.

tasks.short: Identify incoming mail recipients, sort delivery batches, distribute mail, and collect outgoing items.

steps.what: Read recipient names, departments and handling markings on incoming mail.

loop.input: Envelope address images and handling markings; existing structured labels bypass the loop.
loop.output: Recipient name, department and handling flags with image references.
loop.check: Validate fields against the recipient directory; unreadable, conflicting or private markings enter review.
loop.stop: One extraction attempt per envelope; unresolved fields go to the clerk without automatic routing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sender labels vary and may contain free text. Exact matching handles structured labels first.

steps.what: Check the recipient directory and resolve unclear or outdated destinations.
Sort incoming items into recipient or department delivery batches.
Deliver incoming mail to designated desks, mail points or collection areas.
Collect outgoing mail from mail points and return it to the mailroom.

tasks.design: Connect a permitted recipient directory from the {HCM} and location records in the {DOCS} to the {WORKFLOW}. Read structured envelope labels directly and use one bounded extraction loop for irregular addresses, then apply exact routing rules and send ambiguous items to the clerk. The {WORKFLOW} provides ordered delivery lists and collection alerts through the {EMAIL}; physical sorting and movement remain with the clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Envelope formats varied and recipient locations went stale. Physical sorting and delivery still accounted for much of the work.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can handle irregular address text, while deterministic directory matching controls routing. Small integrations are cheaper to build and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Similar names, former employees and confidential markings create exceptions. GDPR applies to envelope images and recipient records; assess the intended use under the EU AI Act and consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous recipients discreetly and recognise items needing special handling without opening private correspondence.

tasks.short: Wrap or tie outgoing packages and bundles securely.

tasks.short: Explain mailing and shipping policies and resolve questions about permitted services.

tasks.design: Configure a structured inquiry form and searchable policy collection in the {HELPDESK} and {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts answers from approved guidance for clerk review, while the {WORKFLOW} sends policy exceptions to the facilities manager before the answer is delivered.

tasks.enabler_now: Search, forms, and approval routing already cover most of the work. A bounded drafting loop can turn retrieved guidance into a clear answer.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting guidance, restricted items, unusual destinations, and requests for policy exceptions still need accountable judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the sender's actual need and explain practical alternatives when the requested service is unsuitable.

tasks.short: Move mail containers safely between internal collection and distribution points using handling equipment.

steps.what: Check collection requests and choose the next container movement.
Inspect handling equipment and check the planned route for hazards.
Load or attach containers and secure them within equipment limits.
Operate handling equipment to move containers to the destination.
Unload or detach containers and place them in the designated receiving area.
Record completed movements and any delivery exceptions in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.design: Configure a collection queue in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with fixed destinations, equipment limits and simple priority rules; the operator confirms the next movement. A short completion form reuses the movement docket and records exceptions without retyping. Physical checks, loading, movement and unloading remain with the operator; no model loop is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most effort is physical. Dispatch and recording improvements alone often did not justify a separate implementation for an occasional task.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configurable queues and forms can reduce paperwork. AI-assisted coding can lower the cost of small configuration extensions, but does not remove physical handling constraints.
tasks.still_hard: Congestion, unstable loads, pedestrians and equipment faults require situational judgement. Driverless movement would need separate equipment, site engineering and safety validation, outside this estimate.
tasks.human_edge: The operator notices unsafe loads and changing floor conditions, stops movement, and coordinates safe passage with nearby people.
tasks.altitude: The operator spends slightly less time choosing jobs and recording completion. Equipment operation dominates the task, so the week and decision rights change little.

tasks.short: Sell mailing supplies and collect postage payments.

steps.what: Ask the requester which mailing supplies and delivery service they need.
Weigh the item and calculate charges using postal equipment and the rate table.
Collect payment through a payment terminal and issue a receipt.
Hand over purchased supplies or accept the paid item for dispatch.
Match daily receipts to payment totals and send discrepancies to finance.

tasks.design: Configure postal equipment in {OTHER} to calculate quotes and pass approved amounts to a payment terminal in {OTHER}. A deterministic integration matches payment records to sales in the {ERP}, replacing the reconciliation workbook in the {SPREADSHEET}; the clerk handles physical items and service questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Postal equipment, payment terminals and finance records often have separate identifiers and exports. Small transaction volumes weaken the case for custom integration.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing rate engines and payment terminals handle the transaction. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building export adapters and reconciliation rules.
tasks.still_hard: Weighing, handing over supplies, unusual items, refunds and cash handling still require attention. Payment equipment may expose only limited interfaces.
tasks.human_edge: Explain service trade-offs and recognise packaging or delivery needs that the requester has described poorly.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time calculating charges and balancing receipts. Service advice and physical handling remain, and decision rights do not change.

tasks.short: Correct legacy address plates used for outgoing mail.

steps.what: Read an address correction request received through the {EMAIL}.
Check the requested correction against the recipient record in the {CRM}.
Use a typewriter or embossing machine to produce the corrected address plate.
Inspect the corrected plate, replace the old plate, and discard it securely.

tasks.design: Replace address plates with labels generated directly from verified recipient records in the {CRM}. Configure an address correction form in the {WORKFLOW}, validate record identifiers deterministically, and require approval before corrected addresses feed the label template in {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: A physical plate library was tied to legacy machinery, while recipient records lived elsewhere. Replacing the addressing method required a small operational migration.
tasks.enabler_now: Ordinary digital label printing removes plate maintenance. A small integration can reuse verified records without retyping addresses.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting address requests need an authorised source. Layout, envelope compatibility and secure disposal of the old plate library need checking.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve conflicting recipient identities and recognise corrections that could send confidential mail to the wrong person.
tasks.altitude: Plate production disappears; the clerk reviews address conflicts and occasional print proofs. Authority to decide disputed recipient data stays with the record owner.
